chapters.label: Intro
chapters.text: Happy Thanksgiving. It's Thursday, November 26th, and this is your short, slightly overfed rundown of what's going on. Plenty to get through before the turkey does its work.

chapters.label: 🌤️ Weather
chapters.text: San Antonio is cloudy and dry today, high of 61, low of 36. It starts chilly at 38, climbs to 57 by midday, then drops to 51 tonight, so layers are your friend. Gusts hit about 21, and it feels like 29 out there early. Friday's 65, Saturday's 73, and no rain until a drizzly Thursday.

chapters.label: 🏆 My Teams
chapters.text: The Spurs dropped one in Portland last night, 116 to 111, their first road loss of the season. Victor Wembanyama did everything he could, 44 points and 16 rebounds, and it still wasn't enough, which feels rude. They're 15 and 4, so nobody's panicking. The Lakers come to San Antonio Friday, and Austin Reaves may play.

chapters.label: 🏆 My Teams
chapters.text: And Cowboys fans, your holiday main course kicks off at 3:30 this afternoon on Fox against the Eagles. Dallas is 5 and 6, Philly is 3 and 7, so yes, it's Thanksgiving and we're all hoping for a good meal and a good second half.

chapters.label: 🇺🇸 U.S.
chapters.text: New York's Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed for the first time ever, and it's the hundredth one, so that's some timing. A powerful coastal storm is headed in with gusts up to 65 miles an hour and possible flash flooding. Now picture giant balloons in that. The new date is Saturday at 8:30 in the morning. Mayor Zohran Mamdani said the city has to plan for every possibility, and Macy's said safety comes first. Honestly, a parade with leftovers on the side sounds like a pretty good upgrade for anyone watching from the couch.  The first postponement in a hundred years is a big deal, but nobody wants a runaway balloon on Sixth Avenue.

chapters.label: 🎬 Culture & Entertainment
chapters.text: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie have finally settled their fight over Château Miraval, the French vineyard where they got married in 2014. It started in 2022, when Pitt sued after Jolie sold her stake to a company controlled by Russian oligarch Yuri Shefler. He said they'd agreed not to sell without each other's permission. She countersued, accusing him of attacking her and their children on a 2016 private flight, which led to her filing for divorce. Both cases are now resolved, and their reps say it was settled for the family's sake with no further comment. They also added that anything attributed to sources isn't coming from either of them, which is a bold claim about the entire celebrity press ecosystem.

chapters.label: 🎬 Culture & Entertainment
chapters.text: Gordon Ramsay is the new face of Top Gear, which has been off the air since 2022, when Andrew Flintoff was seriously injured in a crash at the test track. The BBC apologized and paid him compensation. Filming starts next year, with the return set for 2028, and Ramsay's co-hosts haven't been named yet. He says he grew up near Silverstone and used to sneak in over the fences to watch races. Of all the people you could hand a car show to, he's the one most likely to tell a Lamborghini it's raw. He promises the show will have just the right amount of chaos, which, given its history, is a phrase I'd keep an eye on.

chapters.label: 🌍 World
chapters.text: Here's a good way to deal with something that might explode on its own: explode it yourself, on schedule. This morning the Army is detonating thousands of pounds of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown. It's an explosive used since World War One that was moved to a bunker there 17 years ago, and it crystallized and became unstable. Everyone within five miles has been evacuated, and anyone within twenty miles is told to stay indoors. Also, Kilmar Abrego Garcia, the Salvadoran immigrant who was mistakenly deported in 2025, has left the U.S. for Spain. His lawyer calls it a temporary departure and says he has options to return. And Nvidia's reinstated CEO Jensen Huang reportedly apologized to staff for his past behavior, after stepping down over reports of affairs.

chapters.label: 🏛️ Politics
chapters.text: A federal judge just blocked the FCC, the Federal Communications Commission, from going ahead with an early review of ABC's broadcast licenses. Judge Loren AliKhan wrote a 45-page ruling saying ABC is likely to prove the review was retaliation. She cited at least 11 times President Trump publicly urged the FCC to go after ABC, and said FCC Chair Brendan Carr treated Trump's rhetoric as his marching orders. It's rare for the plaintiff's best evidence to be the defendant's greatest hits. The stakes were big: ABC stations cover six of the ten biggest U.S. markets, including New York, Los Angeles and Houston. Licenses normally run eight years, so an early review was highly unusual. The judge called it not a close case, though she declined a broader ban, and the injunction holds while the lawsuit plays out.

chapters.label: 💻 Tech
chapters.text: The FCC just approved SpaceX's plan to launch up to a million satellites to serve as data centers in orbit. The project is called Starmind. The satellites run on sunlight, crunch AI workloads, and beam the results back down. Nobody wants a data center in their town anymore, and experts say that anger even hurt Republicans in the midterms, so the fix is to put them in everyone's sky. FCC Chair Brendan Carr called it a bold new frontier. Amazon called it a lofty ambition rather than a real plan, and astronomers say it would significantly undermine stargazing. Deployment has to begin by November 2033, so there's time to argue.

chapters.label: ⚡ Quick hits
chapters.text: Quick hits. Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor has died at 65 after a long battle with prostate cancer; he co-wrote Rio, Girls on Film and Save a Prayer, and passed away at home with his family on Monday. In Cairo, a fuel tanker crash set off a huge fire on the ring road and killed at least 31 people, with at least 21 injured. A FedEx plane coming from Memphis overran a runway at Miami's airport last night; nobody was hurt, but there are hours-long delays. Jannik Sinner is out of the Australian Open in January after knee surgery, and he hasn't played since winning Wimbledon in July. And a man in Denver has reportedly been trapping Waymo robotaxis with orange cones and pelting them with eggs; no charges so far.

chapters.label: Wrapping up
chapters.text: That's your Thursday. Eat well, pace yourself during the Cowboys game, and I'll talk to you tomorrow.
